explanation: Both documents reflect a continuation of the existing accommodative stance with no rate changes, no new QE announcements, and no surprise policy shifts; the March 2010 document confirmed the scheduled completion of MBS purchases by end of March and closure of liquidity facilities, which were already well-telegraphed. While the completion of the $1.25 trillion MBS purchase program by end of March 2010 could plausibly have caused a structural break in mortgage or Treasury markets around March 26, this was a pre-announced, widely anticipated event rather than a substantive policy surprise.
